email_and_output_options.title: Email and output options
email_and_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should save output data.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).

input_dataset_options.title: Input datasets
input_dataset_options.description: Sample/dataset paths and ORF coordinate parsing settings. These are normally edited directly in the pipeline's user-input config file rather than passed on the command line.
input_dataset_options.help_text: This section defines which datasets are fed into the pipeline and how ORF (open reading frame) start/stop coordinates are parsed out of each dataset's sequence headers. Both `datasets` and `orf_coord_fields` are edited directly in the `conf/inputs.config` file rather than passed as command-line flags, and can include as many datasets as needed - the naming convention (the keys) is entirely up to the user, but must stay consistent between `datasets` and `orf_coord_fields`.

datasets.description: Map of dataset name to input protein fasta/pep file path, e.g. { ENA: "/path/to/file.pep" }.
datasets.help_text:
Each key is a user-chosen dataset name and each value is the absolute path to that dataset's protein fasta/pep file, for example:

```groovy
datasets = [
  Dataset1: "/absolute/path/to/Dataset1",
  Dataset2: "/absolute/path/to/Dataset2"
]
```

You can add as many dataset entries as needed. Dataset names chosen here are reused later on in `exclude_datasets` and are the keys expected in `orf_coord_fields`.

orf_coord_fields.description: Map of dataset name to the underscore-delimited field index (negative, from the end) holding the ORF start/stop position.
orf_coord_fields.help_text:
Sequence headers are underscore-delimited, and this parameter tells the pipeline which field (counting from the end) contains the ORF start position for each dataset. Use a negative index: -1 is the last field, -2 is the second-to-last field, and so on. For example:

```groovy
orf_coord_fields = [BATS: -2, GOV: -3]
```

Each key must match a dataset name defined in `datasets`.

protein_annotation_options.title: Protein annotation options
protein_annotation_options.description: Reference databases, PFAM annotation, and PASV settings used to detect and annotate marker proteins.
protein_annotation_options.help_text:
PHIDRA conducts homology search and Pfam domain-based validation to identify proteins of interest. Every configured protein passes through PHIDRA validation, and is then assigned a 'genofeature' (the level of genomic information relevant to enzyme biochemistry/phenotype prediction) via one of three methods:

- **PASV proteins** (`pasv_proteins`) are assigned genofeatures based on active site signatures, tuned via `pasv_settings` and `pasv_threshold`.
- **Tophit proteins** (`tophit_proteins`) are assigned genofeatures based on top BLAST hits.
- **Domain proteins** (`domain_proteins`) are assigned genofeatures based on Pfam domain matches, using `pfam_annotation_map`.

Additional proteins can be added to any of these lists, but naming must stay consistent with the corresponding entry in `proteins`.

phidra_dir.description: Path to the Phidra tool/resources directory.
phidra_dir.help_text: Path to the PHIDRA directory, which by default is included inside the pipeline directory. This variable name must remain `phidra_dir` as it is referenced directly in the pipeline code.

pfamDB.description: Path to the Pfam database used for domain annotation.
pfamDB.help_text: Path to the Pfam database, found inside the PHIDRA directory by default. This variable name must remain `pfamDB` as it is referenced directly in the pipeline code.

genofeature_metadata.description: Path to the protein/genofeature metadata file.

proteins.description: List of marker proteins to search for. Each entry defines the protein name, its PFAM domain hit table, subject database for search, and (optionally) a PASV alignment reference file.
proteins.help_text:
Each protein block controls PHIDRA and PASV behaviour for one marker protein. Enter each protein as a separate object in this array.

Required for every protein:
- `protein`: the protein name (must match the corresponding entry in `pasv_proteins`/`tophit_proteins`/`domain_proteins`; case sensitive).
- `pfamDomain`: path to a TSV file of InterPro Domain Architectures, used by PHIDRA.
- `subjectDB`: path to a FASTA file of known proteins used for the PHIDRA homology search.

Additionally required for PASV proteins only:
- `pasv_align_refs`: path to a FASTA file of reference sequences for PASV alignment and active site analysis. VEIL only uses this for RNR and PolA.

Example:
```groovy
proteins = [
  [
    protein: "RNR",
    pfamDomain: "/path/to/pfamDomain.tsv",
    subjectDB: "/path/to/subjectDB.fa",
    pasv_align_refs: "/path/to/pasv_refs.fa"
  ],
  [
    protein: "PolB",
    pfamDomain: "/path/to/pfamDomain.tsv",
    subjectDB: "/path/to/subjectDB.fa"
  ]
]
```

pasv_proteins.description: Proteins (from the `proteins` list) to run PASV on.
pasv_proteins.help_text: Proteins assigned genofeatures via PASV active-site signature analysis. Each entry must also appear in `proteins`, and must have a `pasv_align_refs` file and a corresponding entry in `pasv_settings`.

tophit_proteins.description: Proteins (from the `proteins` list) to annotate via top-hit.
tophit_proteins.help_text: Proteins assigned genofeatures via top-hit annotation. Each entry must also appear in `proteins`.

domain_proteins.description: Proteins (from the `proteins` list) to annotate via domain match.
domain_proteins.help_text: Proteins assigned genofeatures based on Pfam domain match. Each entry must also appear in `proteins`, and must be represented in `pfam_annotation_map`.

pasv_threshold.description: PASV scoring threshold based on decimal values, signatures above the threshold are included if they are not expected signatures.
pasv_threshold.help_text: Expected signatures (`expected_sigs` in `pasv_settings`) are always included in the output when found. Any other signature is also included if it makes up more than this fraction of the total protein data. Given as a decimal (default `0.01` = 1%).

pasv_settings.description: Per-protein PASV settings: mapped_name, region-of-interest start/end, catalytic sites, and expected signatures.
pasv_settings.help_text:
Defines the VEIL standard PASV settings for each PASV protein (currently PolA and RNR), and can be adjusted if needed. For each protein:
- `mapped_name`: display name used for the genofeature.
- `roi_start` / `roi_end`: region-of-interest bounds for the alignment.
- `cat_sites`: comma-separated catalytic site positions.
- `expected_sigs`: list of expected active-site signatures; see `pasv_threshold` for how unexpected signatures are handled.

pfam_annotation_map.description: Map of PFAM accession to annotation label.
pfam_annotation_map.help_text:
Maps each Pfam domain ID to the genofeature name assigned to `domain_proteins` when that domain is matched. Format is genofeature name -> Pfam domain ID, e.g.:

```groovy
pfam_annotation_map = [
  "rPolB" : "PF00136",
  "pPolB" : "PF03175"
]
```

clustering_options.title: Clustering & final analysis options
clustering_options.description: Parameters controlling clustering sweeps and the final-analysis run.
clustering_options.help_text:
Controls the UMAP/HDBSCAN parameter sweep (first/subsequent pipeline runs) and the genofeature-centric final analysis run (`--final_analysis`).

On a clean output directory, the pipeline runs through embedding generation and stops after producing UMAP/HDBSCAN plots across the `nn`/`md`/`mc` sweep. Re-running with existing embeddings in the output directory skips the (resource-intensive) embedding step and regenerates plots directly - useful when adding more `nn`/`md` values. The tiled sweep output can help you pick the `final_nn`/`final_md` values to use for the final analysis.

`final_analysis` should be left `false` in the config; the final analysis run is instead triggered via the `--final_analysis` command-line flag, which regenerates coordinates as needed and produces genofeature-centric plots, applying any `exclude_datasets`/`excluded_genofeatures` filters.

nn.description: Nearest-neighbor values to perform parameter sweep over.
nn.help_text: UMAP nearest-neighbor (`n_neighbors`) values to sweep over, e.g. `nn = [75, 100]`.

md.description: Minimum-distance values to perform parameter sweep over.
md.help_text: UMAP minimum-distance values to sweep over, e.g. `md = [0.3, 0.5, 0.7]`.

mc.description: Minimum cluster size values to sweep over.
mc.help_text: HDBSCAN minimum-cluster size values to sweep over, e.g. `mc = [10, 30]`.

excluded_genofeatures.description: Genofeatures to exclude from the final analysis.
excluded_genofeatures.help_text: Genofeatures to remove from the final analysis and plotting (regenerates UMAP coordinates), e.g. `excluded_genofeatures = ['pPolB', 'PolA']`. Only applies when running with `--final_analysis`.

exclude_datasets.description: Dataset names to exclude from the final analysis.
exclude_datasets.help_text: Dataset names (from `datasets`) to remove from the final analysis and plotting, e.g. `exclude_datasets = ['ENA', 'BATS']`. Only applies when running with `--final_analysis`.

final_md.description: Minimum-distance value used for the final analysis run.
final_md.help_text: The single minimum-distance value used for the genofeature-centric UMAP plot in the final analysis. Chosen based on the results of the `md`/`nn` parameter sweep.

final_nn.description: Nearest-neighbor value used for the final analysis run.
final_nn.help_text: The single nearest-neighbor value used for the genofeature-centric UMAP plot in the final analysis. Chosen based on the results of the `md`/`nn` parameter sweep.

final_analysis.description: Set to run the final analysis stage instead of the parameter sweep.
final_analysis.help_text: Should be left `false` in the config file. Trigger the final analysis run via the `--final_analysis` command-line flag instead of editing this value directly.
